audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[0..6].side all read "Skill" while content win[0..6] and the packet levelChart both read Ahri/Ahri/Ahri/Ahri/Ahri/Ekko/Ekko. The page rendered two different answers to who wins each stage.
audit.why: Content layer and packet agree against a single full-layer field; Ahri's Q (970, 7s flat) and Charm (975, 12s flat) beat Ekko's 325-range E commit until his first item.
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side -> Ahri, phases[5..6].side -> Ekko, with every .why rewritten to argue the same verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] says Charm threatens a kill "the instant she hits 3 items of range advantage" (meaningless); spikes[1] calls Chronobreak a "heal-and-slow"; spikes[2] says "level 6-7 items".
audit.why: Chronobreak heals off damage taken and damages the arrival zone — it has no slow. The level-3 spike is Charm coming online, not an item count.
audit.corrected: Spikes rewritten to level 3 Charm (975 range, cancels E mid-dash), level 6 Spirit Rush three dashes vs Ekko's 110s R, first item flipping the trade with R at 80s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated: Charm "instantly stop[s] movement abilities", so it cancels Ekko's E (Phase Dive) mid-dash. Also missing: Ahri's Q deals true damage on the return pass, so stacking MR does not answer her poke, and Essence Theft heals her back through chip.
audit.why: Riot's own Charm text names the movement-ability stop; the Q text names true damage on the way back; both are absent from every field on the page.
audit.corrected: Stated in enemyWin, tradeGood/tradeBad, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.trading, report[5], dontsFull[0], dontsFull[2], phases[2].why, whys[2] and content early/spikes.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: It is the field that must hold real numbers.
audit.corrected: Charm 12s flat at every rank, Orb of Deception 7s flat, Chronobreak 110/80/50.

audit.whatIsWrong: 19 lint findings: 14 misgenderings of Ahri as he/his/him, 2 copy-paste bleeds (dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d verbatim tradeGood/tradeBad), 1 cooldown field with no number.
audit.why: Deterministically detected; Ahri is she/her per champ-gender.js.
audit.corrected: All fixed in the edits below.

edits.before: Ahri's Orb of Deception poke chunks you for free from level 1-2, and once she hits level 3 the Charm-into-full-combo threat means you have to play the lane from max range, giving up CS or eating chip damage every time you push. Your Timewinder (Q) trades evenly at best, but you lack the burst to punish her positioning before level 6, so you're mostly surviving and looking for a W stun on her cooldowns.
edits.after: Ahri's Orb of Deception chunks you for free from level 1-2 — magic on the way out, true damage back, so MR does not answer it — and at 3 her Charm cancels your E mid-dash, so every step forward runs on her 12s timer. Your Timewinder (Q) outranges her at 1075 but you lack the burst before 6, so you farm the wave and look for the W stun in the window after she throws Charm. Her Essence Theft heal pays back your chip every nine minions.

edits.before: Spirit Rush at 6 lets Ahri reposition through your stun and Charm setups, so her all-in window is genuinely scary even though your kit comes online too — she can flash-adjacent an escape or engage that you can't easily punish with just Chronobreak's heal-and-slow. You need to bait out her dashes with W (Parallel Convergence) placement and only commit when she's spent Charm or is out of Spirit Rush charges.
edits.after: Spirit Rush at 6 gives Ahri three dashes to leave your W stun and re-angle Charm, so her all-in window is real even as your kit comes online — Chronobreak heals the damage back but does not undo the Charm that started the chain. Bait the dashes by placing Parallel Convergence early rather than reactively, and only commit when Charm is spent or she is out of Spirit Rush charges.

notes:
CHART: full-layer phases[].side was 'Skill' on all seven rows while content win[] and packet.levelChart both read Ahri x5 / Ekko x2 — a cross-layer disagreement on every row. I moved the full layer to match the content layer, so no win[N] edits were possible (before would equal after and the applier would reject them); the pair is already consistent once these land. Every side edit ships with its .why rewritten to argue the same verdict. Ratings moved 5/10 -> 4/10 on rows 0-3 only; phases[4..6] ratings left as-is since the chart direction there was already 5-6/10.

DECISIVE INTERACTION added everywhere: Charm 'instantly stop[s] movement abilities' per Riot's own text, so it cancels Ekko's E mid-dash. Also added: Q's return pass is true damage (stacking MR is the wrong buy) and Essence Theft heals her through chip (Grievous Wounds timing) — both flagged in missingInteractions and absent from the page.

REPORT SWEEP: I rewrote only report[5] substantively. report[0]/[1]/[3]/[4]/[9] are pronoun-only corrections for the lint MISGENDER findings, not sweep rewrites.

LEFT ALONE (templated but not groundable in Ahri's kit without inventing): breakdown.carry ('one carry per rewind cycle'), breakdown.feeding, breakdown.mid, breakdown.late, late (content). Nothing in the kit gives an Ahri-specific fact for those beyond what I already used elsewhere.

UNVERIFIED, not written: whether Ekko's W anomaly stun can catch Ahri mid-Spirit Rush dash, and whether Charm's movement-ability stop applies to Ekko's E during the dash portion or only before it. Riot's text says 'instantly stopping movement abilities'; I wrote the interaction at that level of generality and did not claim frame-level behaviour.
